Pancakes are tasty. They can be frozen for easy breakfast. I made a giant stack today so no one will bother me for a while. I will share a recipe stolen from somewhere forgotten on the Internets.

Thick Fluffy Pancakes

Equipment:

  • Scale
  • 2 x Mixing bowl
  • Paddle for mixing
  • Griddle preferred because these cook slow so being able to make 3 or 4 at a time is good but good skillet will do.
  • Something to sift flour

Ingredients:

  • 7oz Flour
  • 1oz Sugar
  • 1/2 oz Baking Powder
  • 1/4 oz salt
  • 2 medium to large eggs
  • 8 1/2 oz milk ( you can use water but milk is better. sour milk is fine too)
  • 2 oz butter

Preparation: will make six pancakes about 1 1/2 inch thick each

  • Melt butter and set on side to cool, You'll use it later.
  • Preheat your griddle or skillet. You will be cooking on low heat.
  • Sift into 1st bowl flour, sugar, baking powder, salt. If you are using sea salt, you may want to grind it first. Mix.
  • In 2nd bowl, combine eggs and milk together. Mix lightly with a fork.
  • Combine contents of bowl 1 and 2. Do not use a whisk. Use a paddle or spatula to fold ingredients till all flour is mixed. Rough mixing will cause gluten to form and make the pancakes tougher.
  • Add melted butter to batter. Fold in gently.
  • Use a laddle or cup to scoop batter. It don't pour too good.
  • Put batter on dry pan. Cook for about 2-3 minutes on each side. Cakes need time to rise that is why we are cooking on low heat.
  • Let cakes cool before putting in freezer.
